notes: dateText reads 8:21 PM for a message sent at 20:20:39. Outlook desktop rounds the quoted time to the nearest minute where every other client truncates, so an inline-extracted timestamp can land in the following minute.
text/plain and text/html are both base64. Searching raw bytes for cid: or for a separator finds nothing; parts must be decoded first.
The subject mixes encodings within one header: =?utf-8?B?...?= followed by =?utf-8?Q?...?=. Charset and encoding are per encoded word, not per header.
Content-Disposition carries a size= parameter alongside filename=.
The forward prefix is uppercase FW: here and mixed-case Fw: from Outlook web.
